title: Catch PNG and large-ID photo display filename regressions
scope:
Test-only implementation: extend server/__tests__/photo-delete.test.ts with serial backend cases calling the REAL storage.atomicCreatePhoto method from server/storage.ts. Preserve all existing tests. Do not change production code, package scripts, tier workloads, gate policy, storage or upload security, migrations, browser fixtures, or the separately sealed mobile JPEG handoff and sign-in repairs. The route in server/routes.ts extracts the last extension with (originalFilename || "photo.jpg").match(/\.[^.]+$/)?.[0] || ".jpg"; this plan tests its existing .jpg and .png outputs at the storage boundary, not HTTP handler extraction. Do not copy the filename implementation into a fake storage method or derive expected values from the result under test.

## Fixture design
Use a UUID-named disposable PostgreSQL schema, following the release-schema export isolation pattern in server/__tests__/integrity-release-schema.test.ts and isolatedPool pattern in server/__tests__/routes.test.ts. Export the reviewed shared/schema.ts with the existing drizzle-kit export --sql --dialect postgresql --schema ./shared/schema.ts command under an explicit 30000 ms subprocess timeout; retarget quoted public-qualified references to the disposable schema, including foreign keys, and execute the export only there. Do not prepend enum DDL. Use a dedicated pg.Pool whose search_path is exclusively that schema, and drizzle(isolatedPool, { schema: databaseSchema }). Patch only the imported db.transaction method with the serial test context's mock facility to delegate to isolatedDb.transaction, forwarding options and callback; the REAL atomicCreatePhoto transaction callback, queries, conflict target, row update and intent consumption must execute in PostgreSQL. No other test may overlap the patch, and restore it before dropping the schema. Create session and upload-intent fixtures with matching user ownership, unique registration keys, and canonical /uploads/ object paths. The schema owns its sequences: set the isolated photos sequence via pg_get_serial_sequence on its explicitly qualified table and setval(..., desiredId, false). Never setval, restart, truncate, or insert forced IDs into shared/public tables. Insert explicit fixture session IDs 7 and 12345 in the isolated schema. Delete each case's isolated photo and intent rows before reseeding its sequence so repeated combinations cannot conflict. Do not create, upload, rename, or delete physical blobs. Assert the returned photo ID matches the seeded ID before checking its name. Keep the suite serial and bounded (120000 ms suite deadline with bounded database connection/query waits); close the dedicated pool, drop only the uniquely owned schema, release setup clients, and restore mocks in finally/after cleanup even on partial setup or assertion failure. Preserve the existing shared pool teardown. If isolation cannot be made faithful, pause and amend through the supported route rather than adding a production dependency-injection seam or falling back to shared sequence mutation.

## Planned cases
For each session ID 7 and 12345 and each extension .jpg and .png, exercise photo IDs 1, 42, 9999, 10000 and 123456. Use an explicit expected photo-token table: 1 => 0001, 42 => 0042, 9999 => 9999, 10000 => 10000, 123456 => 123456. Compose expected strings from fixture session ID, literal token and extension; do not use padStart or slice in the test oracle. Examples include S7_P0001.png, S7_P0042.jpg, S12345_P9999.png, S12345_P10000.jpg and S12345_P123456.png. In all 20 combinations, require exact originalFilename on the returned photo AND an independent SELECT through isolatedDb. Require sessionId and id to match fixtures, originalFilename to differ from the source name, and returned/persisted objectStorageKey to equal the original unique /uploads/ path byte-for-byte, not a path derived from the generated name. Assert successful registration consumes the owned upload intent. Retry the same registration and assert the same ID, exact generated filename, unchanged object key and exactly one persisted photo for that registration; do not weaken existing ownership or retry coverage.

## Detection and handoff
The literal-token oracle must fail for source-name passthrough, missing padding, zero-padding the session ID, hardcoded .jpg, four-digit truncation and display-name-based physical key rewriting. Establish this by assertion-level counterexample reasoning in the delivery handoff, or an isolated negative-control fixture confined to test data; never mutate production code or live resources to demonstrate failure. Map R1-R4 to actual case names/assertions and observed assigned-tier results. No independent verification is selected. Planning readiness is not delivered test coverage or an application-tier PASS. Subsequent implementation requires applicable owner authorization for this sealed revision and a fresh Agent-first guard.

## Regression Guard
**Self-satisfying** — The entire implementation scope is the test/check itself: server/__tests__/photo-delete.test.ts, atomicCreatePhoto exact generated filename cases for .jpg/.png with session IDs 7/12345 and photo IDs 1/42/9999/10000/123456; returned and persisted name, unchanged physical key, consumed intent and idempotent retry assertions. No separate material behavior change is included.
why: The unchanged test-standard unit-tests step executes server/__tests__/photo-delete.test.ts, covering real backend naming and isolated PostgreSQL persistence; test-fast has no application unit-tests step and cannot execute these cases.
coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json tiers.test-standard, all 8 steps and 300000 ms bound: typecheck, storage-lint, port-reference-scan, storage-lint-contract, unit-tests, clerk-release-contract, vite-hmr-tests, manifest-parity. package.json test:unit explicitly includes server/__tests__/photo-delete.test.ts and integrity-release-schema.test.ts, whose existing export fixture demonstrates the supported schema-isolation approach. No new test file registration or workload change is needed. Test TypeScript files are excluded by tsconfig.json, so typecheck alone does not certify these backend cases; execution by unit-tests supplies their assertions. Before implementation use TASK_ID and TASK_PLAN_FILE with npm run gate:guard -- --tier test-standard; after implementation use the full generated bound-tier gate:run command. Optional supported --step unit-tests diagnostics retain task context but do not replace the full tier. Planning inspects source only: no DB, provider, compiler, unit, browser, or application workload is run. Future execution needs the configured PostgreSQL database and disposable-schema privileges; availability was not probed here. If unavailable, report BLOCKED without weakening isolation or changing tier. Unrelated failures follow the baseline classification policy, not automatic waivers.
